learning: Baseline only. To check first: whether kd = 0.2 is enough to stop oscillation on the slalom, and whether base_speed = 1.6 holds the line on the tight bends of the s-bend track.
notes: Baseline integration of the Builder's symmetric five-sensor row with a conservative proportional-derivative controller. Weights follow sensor lateral position, and line loss recovers toward the last seen side. No race data yet, so gains are untuned.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data, so the controller is a conservative first design for the Builder's symmetric five-sensor baseline. Sensor x-positions are -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04 (positive = left). Weights are set proportional to each sensor's lateral position (-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1). A line to the left of centre then gives a positive signal, which steers left, as the contract requires. The centre sensor has weight 0, so a centred robot gives signal 0. kp = 2 gives a turn of about 1 to 2 for signals near 0.5 to 1, i.e. 350 to 700 PWM of differential, which is firm without being violent. ki = 0 avoids integral windup on a 3 s run. kd = 0.2 damps the steering and limits oscillation, the main risk the Builder's notes flag. base_speed = 1.6 (PWM about 80 percent) is a moderate speed. It should reach the 1.5 m/s average needed without pushing the robot into the off-track limit on the sharpest bend. line_loss = last_direction, so the robot keeps turning toward the side it last saw the line. Expected result: completion on the development tracks with few line-loss events. I have not measured this, so the first race will decide whether kp, kd or base_speed need to move.
